question: Which of the following statements is true for a concave lens?
option_1: Image is much larger than object
option_3: Image is always virtual, erect, and on the same side as the object
option_4: Image is always virtual and on the opposite side
solution_text:
The correct answer is Image is always virtual, erect, and on the same side as the object.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A concave lens (diverging lens) always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image on the same side as the object, no matter where the object is placed. (अवतल लेंस — सदैव आभासी, सीधा प्रतिबिम्ब)

 

• This happens because a concave lens diverges parallel rays of light outward; the refracted rays never actually meet, so they are extended backward to locate the virtual image, which always lies between the lens and its focus.

 

• As the object is moved farther from the lens, the image becomes smaller and moves closer to the focus, but it never becomes real or inverted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• A convex lens, by contrast, can form either a real, inverted image or a virtual, erect image, depending on the object's position relative to the focus.

 

• The power of a concave lens is negative (measured in dioptres, D = 1/f in metres), while that of a convex lens is positive.

 

• Concave lenses are used to correct myopia (near-sightedness).

 

NOTE

 

• Image is much larger than object (Option A): True only for a convex lens with the object between the focus and the lens.

 

• Image is always real (Option B): A concave lens never forms a real image; only a convex lens can, under certain conditions.

 

• Image is always virtual and on the opposite side (Option D): Incorrect — the virtual image formed by a concave lens lies on the same side as the object, not the opposite side.

question: Which of the following correctly identifies a solution where the solute and solvent are both elements, and the solution is homogeneous?
option_2: Oxygen mixed with Nitrogen in air
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oxygen mixed with Nitrogen in air.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Air is a homogeneous solution in which both oxygen (solute) and nitrogen (solvent, being present in the largest proportion) are elements, uniformly mixed at the molecular level. (वायु — तत्वों का समांगी मिश्रण)

 

• A homogeneous mixture (solution) has a uniform composition and properties throughout; its components cannot be seen separately, even under a microscope.

 

• For a solution to have 'both solute and solvent as elements', both substances must appear on the Periodic Table as elements — oxygen and nitrogen both qualify, since air is mostly a gaseous solution of these two elements plus small amounts of other gases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A solution always has two parts: the solute (present in smaller quantity, gets dissolved) and the solvent (present in larger quantity, does the dissolving).

 

• Common gaseous solutions: air (O₂ + N₂ + others), while common liquid solutions include sugar or salt in water.

 

• Alloys like brass (copper + zinc) and bronze (copper + tin) are solid solutions of two or more metals (elements).

 

NOTE

 

• Carbon dissolved in water (Option A): Carbon does not dissolve in water at all; this is not even a valid solution.

 

• Iron filings mixed with Sulphur (Option C): This is a heterogeneous mixture, not a solution — the two components remain visibly distinct and can be separated using a magnet.

 

• Sugar dissolved in water (Option D): A genuine homogeneous solution, but sugar (a compound, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is not an element, so it does not satisfy the condition of both solute and solvent being elements.

question: For concave mirror, the height of an image above the principal axis _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is is considered positive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By the Cartesian sign convention used for spherical mirrors, all heights measured upward, above the principal axis, are taken as positive, and all heights measured downward, below the principal axis, are taken as negative. (कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी — प्रधान अक्ष के ऊपर की ऊँचाई धनात्मक)

 

• This convention is applied regardless of the type of mirror (concave or convex) — it is simply a rule for measuring distances and heights consistently in the mirror formula and magnification formula.

 

• Since the question asks specifically about height measured above the principal axis, by definition this is always taken as positive, whether the resulting image itself is virtual/erect (object within focus) or real/inverted with part of the object above the axis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the same convention: distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, and those measured against it are negative; the pole of the mirror is taken as the origin.

 

• Magnification (m) = −v/u = h′/h; a positive value of m indicates a virtual, erect image, while a negative value indicates a real, inverted image.

 

• For a concave mirror, the focal length is taken as negative, while for a convex mirror it is positive, since the focus of a concave mirror lies in front of the mirror (real side).

 

NOTE

 

• Depends on object position (Option A): Incorrect — the sign convention for height depends only on direction (above/below axis), not on where the object is placed.

 

• Is considered zero (Option B): Incorrect — a height above the axis is never taken as zero unless there genuinely is no image.

 

• Is considered negative (Option D): This would apply to heights measured below the principal axis, not above it.

question: Which functional group present in aldehyde?
solution_text:
The correct answer is -CHO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The aldehyde functional group is -CHO (the carbonyl carbon bonded to a hydrogen atom), and it is always found at the end (terminal) carbon of the carbon chain. (एल्डिहाइड समूह — -CHO)

 

• Compounds containing this group are named with the suffix '-al', for example, methanal (formaldehyde, HCHO) and ethanal (acetaldehyde, CH₃CHO).

 

• Aldehydes are formed by the partial oxidation of primary alcohols, and further oxidation of an aldehyde converts it into the corresponding carboxylic acid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• -CO- (Option A) represents the ketone (carbonyl) group, found between two carbon atoms (never at the end); ketone names carry the suffix '-one', e.g. propanone (acetone).

 

• Both aldehydes and ketones contain the carbonyl group (C=O), which is why they are collectively called carbonyl compounds; the difference is only in what is attached to that carbon.

 

• A simple test to distinguish aldehydes from ketones is Tollens' reagent (silver mirror test) — aldehydes give a shiny silver deposit, ketones do not.

 

NOTE

 

• -CO (Option A): The ketone functional group, not aldehyde.

 

• -COOH (Option C): The carboxylic acid functional group; compounds are named with the suffix '-oic acid'.

 

• -OH (Option D): The hydroxyl (alcohol) functional group; compounds are named with the suffix '-ol'.

question: A body moves along a straight line with varying speed. Its displacement in 10 s is 50 m. What is the average velocity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 m/s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Average velocity is defined as total displacement divided by total time taken, irrespective of how the speed varied during the journey. (औसत वेग = कुल विस्थापन / कुल समय)

 

• Here, displacement = 50 m and time = 10 s, so average velocity = 50 ÷ 10 = 5 m/s.

 

• Average velocity depends only on the initial and final positions (net displacement), not on the actual path or how speed changed in between — that distinction belongs to average speed, which uses total distance travelled.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Average speed = total distance ÷ total time; it is always positive and can differ from average velocity if the body changes direction.

 

• Velocity is a vector quantity (has both magnitude and direction), while speed is a scalar quantity (magnitude only).

 

• If a body returns to its starting point, its displacement is zero, so its average velocity is zero — even though it may have covered a large distance.

 

NOTE

 

• 25 m/s (Option B) and 50 m/s (Option C): These would result from dividing incorrectly (e.g. multiplying instead of dividing, or using only half the time).

 

• 10 m/s (Option D): This is not obtained by the correct formula 50 ÷ 10; it is a distractor value.

question: Which of the following statements correctly describes a typical physical property of metals?
option_1: Metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity.
option_2: Metals are sonorous and produce sound when struck.
option_3: Metals have low melting and boiling points.
option_4: Metals are generally brittle and break easily when hammered.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Metals are sonorous and produce sound when struck.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonorousness is a characteristic physical property of metals — when struck, metals produce a ringing sound, which is why metals like bronze and brass are used to make bells and other musical instruments. (धात्विक ध्वनि गुण — sonorous)

 

• This property arises from the closely packed, orderly arrangement of metal atoms held together by strong metallic bonds, which allows metals to vibrate and produce sound when struck rather than shattering.

 

• Along with sonorousness, metals typically show malleability (can be beaten into thin sheets) and ductility (can be drawn into wires) — both a result of the same metallic bonding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metals are generally good conductors of heat and electricity because of the presence of free (delocalised) electrons in their structure.

 

• Most metals have high melting and boiling points (exceptions include mercury, gallium, and sodium/potassium, which have relatively low melting points).

 

• Non-metals, by contrast, are typically brittle (break into pieces when hammered) — this property is called the opposite of malleability.

 

NOTE

 

• Metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity (Option A): Incorrect — this describes non-metals, not metals.

 

• Metals have low melting and boiling points (Option C): Incorrect as a general rule — most metals (like iron, at 1538°C) have high melting points.

 

• Metals are generally brittle and break easily when hammered (Option D): Incorrect — this describes non-metals; metals are malleable, not brittle.

question: Which of the following is true about heterogeneous mixtures?
option_2: The composition is the same throughout
option_3: The individual substances retain their properties
solution_text:
The correct answer is The individual substances retain their properties.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a heterogeneous mixture, the components are not uniformly distributed, remain visibly distinct, and each substance retains its own physical and chemical properties even after mixing. (विषमांगी मिश्रण — घटक अपने गुण बनाए रखते हैं)

 

• Examples include a mixture of sand and salt, oil and water, or iron filings and sulphur — in each case, you can identify the individual substances and, in principle, separate them using appropriate physical methods (filtration, sieving, use of a magnet, etc.).

 

• This is a defining difference from a compound, where the constituent elements lose their original properties entirely and form a new substance with fixed composition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mixtures can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, evaporation, distillation, sublimation, chromatography, and magnetic separation — no chemical reaction is required.

 

• A homogeneous mixture (solution) has uniform composition throughout and cannot be visually distinguished into separate components.

 

• Colloids and suspensions are special types of heterogeneous mixtures with intermediate particle sizes between true solutions and ordinary heterogeneous mixtures.

 

NOTE

 

• The components cannot be separated (Option A): Incorrect — a key feature of any mixture (homogeneous or heterogeneous) is that its components CAN be separated by physical means.

 

• The composition is the same throughout (Option B): This describes a homogeneous mixture, not a heterogeneous one.

 

• It behaves like a compound (Option D): Incorrect — a mixture, unlike a compound, does not have fixed proportions or new properties distinct from its constituents.

question: Ethanol is miscible with water due to presence of which functional group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydroxyl group.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) contains the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group, which is able to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making ethanol completely miscible (soluble in all proportions) with water. (हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह — जल में घुलनशीलता)

 

• The polar -OH group behaves similarly to the -OH in water itself, so ethanol molecules readily mix with water at the molecular level rather than forming a separate layer.

 

• As the length of the hydrocarbon (non-polar) chain in an alcohol increases, its solubility in water decreases, because the non-polar part starts to dominate over the polar -OH group's water-attracting effect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ethanol is manufactured industrially by the fermentation of sugars (using yeast, which produces the enzyme zymase) and is also used as a solvent, in medicines, and as a biofuel/fuel additive.

 

• Hydrogen bonding is a special, relatively strong intermolecular force that occurs between molecules with an -OH or -NH group and is responsible for water's unusually high boiling point.

 

• Denatured alcohol is ethanol mixed with a poisonous substance (like methanol) to make it unfit for drinking while still being usable industrially.

 

NOTE

 

• Double bond (Option A): Ethanol does not contain a carbon-carbon double bond; it is a saturated compound.

 

• Carbon chain (Option C): The hydrocarbon (ethyl) part of ethanol is actually non-polar and tends to reduce water solubility, not increase it.

 

• Carboxyl group (Option D): This is the -COOH group found in carboxylic acids (like acetic acid), not in ethanol.

question: What happens to the density of a substance when the temperature of a substance increases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Density decreases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When the temperature of a substance increases, it generally expands (its volume increases) while its mass stays constant, so its density (mass ÷ volume) decreases. (घनत्व = द्रव्यमान/आयतन — तापमान बढ़ने पर घनत्व घटता है)

 

• This happens because heating increases the kinetic energy of particles, causing them to vibrate more and move slightly farther apart, thereby increasing the volume occupied by the same mass of substance.

 

• This principle explains phenomena like hot air balloons rising (hot air is less dense than the surrounding cooler air) and convection currents in fluids.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Water shows an exception near 4°C — it has its maximum density at 4°C, and further cooling to 0°C actually causes it to expand slightly (this is why ice floats on water), a phenomenon called the anomalous expansion of water.

 

• The general order of density is solids > liquids > gases, because particles are most closely packed in solids and most loosely packed (widely spaced) in gases.

 

• Density = Mass/Volume, with SI unit kg/m³ (commonly expressed as g/cm³ for smaller objects).

 

NOTE

 

• Density increases (Option B): Incorrect — the opposite of what generally happens; occurs only in exceptional cases like water cooling from 4°C down to 0°C.

 

• Density doubles (Option C): There is no universal rule that density exactly doubles with a temperature rise; the change depends on the material's coefficient of expansion.

 

• Density has no effect (Option D): Incorrect — temperature does affect density through thermal expansion (or contraction).

question: The DNA in the cell nucleus is the information source for the making of which of the following substances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protein.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid), present in the cell nucleus, carries the genetic code that determines the sequence of amino acids in a protein, through the processes of transcription (DNA → mRNA) and translation (mRNA → protein at the ribosome). (डीएनए — प्रोटीन संश्लेषण की सूचना)

 

• Each gene is a segment of DNA that codes for one particular protein (or polypeptide chain); the sequence of nitrogenous bases (A, T, G, C) in DNA determines the exact sequence of amino acids.

 

• Proteins produced this way perform vital roles as enzymes, hormones, structural components (like keratin, collagen), and antibodies, making this DNA-to-protein pathway fundamental to how genes control the traits and functioning of an organism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The flow of genetic information — DNA → RNA → Protein — is known as the Central Dogma of Molecular Biology, first proposed by Francis Crick.

 

• DNA is a double helix structure, discovered by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, made of two strands held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs (A-T and G-C).

 

• RNA (Ribonucleic Acid) acts as the intermediary messenger that carries the genetic code from DNA in the nucleus to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm, where protein synthesis actually occurs.

 

NOTE

 

• Glucose (Option A) and Fructose (Option B): These are simple sugars (carbohydrates) produced through metabolic pathways like photosynthesis or digestion, not directly coded for by DNA.

 

• Lipid (Option D): Lipids (fats) are synthesised through enzymatic pathways, but DNA does not directly template lipid structure the way it does for proteins.

question: A man undergoes a minor surgical procedure that prevents sperm from mixing with semen. Which structure was most likely altered?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vas deferens.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The procedure described is a vasectomy, a permanent contraceptive method in which the vas deferens — the tube that carries sperm from the epididymis to the urethra — is cut and sealed. (शुक्रवाहिका — नसबंदी में काटी जाती है)

 

• After a vasectomy, sperm can no longer travel from the testes to mix with the fluid secreted by the seminal vesicles and prostate gland, so the semen ejaculated contains no sperm, even though sexual function and ejaculation continue normally.

 

• The testes continue to produce sperm as usual, but the sperm are simply reabsorbed by the body since they cannot travel further along the blocked vas deferens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The female equivalent permanent contraceptive procedure is called tubectomy (tubal ligation), in which the fallopian tubes are cut/blocked to prevent the egg from meeting sperm.

 

• Semen is a mixture of sperm (from the testes) and secretions from the seminal vesicles, prostate gland, and bulbourethral glands, which nourish and help transport the sperm.

 

• Both vasectomy and tubectomy are considered highly effective, permanent methods of birth control (family planning).

 

NOTE

 

• Urethra (Option B): The common tube through which both urine and semen pass out of the body; it is not typically cut in a vasectomy.

 

• Testis (Option C): The gland where sperm are actually produced; it is left intact so sperm production continues.

 

• Penis (Option D): The external reproductive organ used for copulation and passing urine/semen; it is not altered in a vasectomy.

question: Which of the following helps in maintaining reproductive health?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Health education and medical care.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reproductive health refers to complete physical, mental and social well-being in matters related to the reproductive system, and it is best maintained through proper health education, awareness, hygiene practices, and access to medical care and checkups. (प्रजनन स्वास्थ्य — स्वास्थ्य शिक्षा एवं चिकित्सा देखभाल)

 

• Health education helps individuals understand safe practices, prevent sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and make informed decisions about family planning and contraception.

 

• Regular medical care and checkups enable the early detection and treatment of reproductive health issues, ensuring safe pregnancies and overall wellness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Government programmes like the National Health Mission and school-level Adolescence Education Programme (AEP) aim to spread awareness about reproductive and sexual health among the youth.

 

• Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) such as HIV/AIDS, gonorrhoea and syphilis can be prevented by using barrier methods like condoms, alongside safe practices and hygiene.

 

• Family planning methods (natural, barrier, hormonal, and surgical) help control population growth and support reproductive health.

 

NOTE

 

• Junk food (Option A): Poor nutrition negatively affects overall health, including reproductive health, rather than maintaining it.

 

• Early marriage (Option B): Early marriage and early pregnancy are associated with health risks for both mother and child and are generally discouraged for maintaining good reproductive health.

 

• Ignoring hygiene (Option D): Poor hygiene increases the risk of reproductive tract infections; good hygiene is essential, not something to be ignored.

question: Which part of the neuron contains the nucleus and the cytoplasm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell body.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cell body (cyton/soma) of a neuron contains the nucleus and most of the cytoplasm, along with other cell organelles such as mitochondria and the Nissl granules (rough endoplasmic reticulum). (कोशिकाकाय — केंद्रक एवं कोशिकाद्रव्य)

 

• The cell body is the metabolic centre of the neuron, responsible for maintaining the cell and synthesising proteins and neurotransmitters needed by the rest of the neuron.

 

• From the cell body extend the dendrites (which receive signals) and a single long axon (which transmits signals away from the cell body to other neurons or effector organs).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• A neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system; nerve impulses travel as electrochemical signals along the neuron.

 

• The junction between two neurons, where a nerve impulse is transmitted (via neurotransmitter chemicals) from one to the next, is called a synapse.

 

• Many axons are covered by a fatty insulating sheath called the myelin sheath, which speeds up the conduction of nerve impulses.

 

NOTE

 

• Axon (Option B): A long, thin projection from the cell body that carries nerve impulses away from the cell body; it does not contain the nucleus.

 

• Dendrites (Option C): Short, branched extensions that receive incoming nerve impulses and carry them toward the cell body; they also lack the nucleus.

 

• Nerve endings (Option D): The terminal branches of the axon that release neurotransmitters at the synapse; they are far from the nucleus, which resides only in the cell body.

question: Which of the following quantities does NOT affect the buoyant force acting on a body immersed in a fluid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Density of object.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The buoyant force (upthrust) on a body immersed in a fluid is given by Archimedes' Principle: F = ρ(fluid) × V(displaced) × g, which depends only on the density of the fluid, the volume of fluid displaced, and gravitational acceleration (g) — the object's own density does not appear in this formula. (उत्प्लावन बल — वस्तु के घनत्व पर निर्भर नहीं करता)

 

• The density of the object determines whether the object floats or sinks (by comparison with the fluid's density) and how much of it gets submerged, but it does not directly change the magnitude of the buoyant force formula itself once the displaced volume is fixed.

 

• In other words, two objects of the same volume immersed in the same fluid experience the same buoyant force, regardless of what they are made of (i.e., regardless of their own density).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Archimedes' Principle: When a body is partially or fully immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.

 

• A body floats if its average density is less than or equal to that of the fluid, and sinks if its density is greater.

 

• This principle is used in designing ships, submarines, hydrometers, and in determining the purity of substances (e.g. testing milk purity with a lactometer).

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of displaced fluid (Option A): Directly proportional to buoyant force — more fluid displaced means greater upthrust.

 

• Gravitational acceleration (Option C): Buoyant force is directly proportional to 'g'; on the Moon, buoyant force on the same object in the same fluid would be about one-sixth of that on Earth.

 

• Density of fluid (Option D): Directly proportional to buoyant force — this is why objects float more easily in denser fluids (e.g. it's easier to float in seawater than in fresh water).

question: Which of the following statements about adrenaline is INCORRECT?
option_1: It promotes digestion by increasing blood flow to the stomach.
option_2: It helps the body respond to stress or emergency by triggering the ‘fight or flight’ response.
option_3: It reduces blood supply to the digestive system and directs it toward the skeletal muscles.
option_4: It increases heart rate and breathing rate to supply more oxygen to the muscles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It promotes digestion by increasing blood flow to the stomach.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Adrenaline (epinephrine), secreted by the adrenal glands, is the body's 'emergency hormone' — during stress, it actually decreases blood flow to the digestive system (since digestion is not urgent in an emergency) and redirects that blood toward the skeletal muscles, so Statement A is factually incorrect and is therefore the answer. (एड्रेनालिन — 'लड़ो या भागो' हार्मोन)

 

• Adrenaline triggers the classic 'fight or flight' response, preparing the body to either confront a threat or flee from it, by rapidly mobilising the body's resources.

 

• Its actions include increased heart rate, increased breathing rate, dilated pupils, raised blood sugar level, and redirection of blood flow away from non-essential functions (like digestion) and toward the muscles, heart and brain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer (the INCORRECT statement) is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal medulla (the inner part of the adrenal gland, located above each kidney); it is sometimes called the 'hormone of emergency'.

 

• Adrenaline works alongside the sympathetic nervous system to produce rapid, short-term bodily changes in response to sudden stress or danger.

 

• Its close relative, noradrenaline (norepinephrine), also plays a role in the stress response and acts as both a hormone and a neurotransmitter.

 

NOTE

 

• Helps the body respond to stress ... 'fight or flight' (Option B): This is a correct, textbook description of adrenaline's primary role.

 

• Reduces blood supply to the digestive system ... skeletal muscles (Option C): Correct — exactly the opposite of what Option A claims, which is why Option A is false.

 

• Increases heart rate and breathing rate (Option D): Correct — adrenaline stimulates the heart and lungs to supply extra oxygen to the muscles during an emergency.

question: The work required by an external force to bring a moving body to rest is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is its kinetic energy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By the work-energy theorem, the work done by a force on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy. To bring a moving body to rest, its final kinetic energy becomes zero, so the work required equals its initial kinetic energy. (कार्य-ऊर्जा प्रमेय — कार्य = गतिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन)

 

• Mathematically, Work done = ΔKE = KE(final) − KE(initial) = 0 − ½mv² = −½mv². The magnitude of work that the external (opposing) force must do is therefore ½mv², i.e., equal to the body's kinetic energy.

 

• This is why brakes on a vehicle heat up — the work done by friction to stop the vehicle converts its kinetic energy into heat energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kinetic energy (KE) = ½mv², where m is mass and v is velocity; it is a scalar quantity, always positive, and depends on the square of velocity.

 

• Potential energy is energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration (e.g. gravitational PE = mgh), and is unrelated to a body's motion.

 

• Momentum (p = mv) is a vector quantity representing the quantity of motion, distinct in units and nature from work/energy (which are scalar quantities).

 

NOTE

 

• Its weight (Option A): Weight (W = mg) is a force, not a form of work or energy relevant to stopping a moving body.

 

• Its momentum (Option B): Momentum has units of kg·m/s, different from the units of work/energy (joules); stopping a body relates to energy, not directly to momentum.

 

• Its potential energy (Option C): Potential energy depends on position, not motion, so it is not what determines the work needed to stop a moving object.

question: The working principle of a stethoscope is based on the _______.
option_1: conversion of sound into electric signals only
option_4: conversion of sound into light for observation
solution_text:
The correct answer is reflection of sound.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A stethoscope works on the principle of multiple/total internal reflection of sound waves — the sound produced inside the body (like the heartbeat) travels through the tubes of the stethoscope by repeatedly reflecting off the inner walls, so that almost no sound energy is lost before it reaches the doctor's ears. (स्टेथोस्कोप — ध्वनि के परावर्तन पर आधारित)

 

• This makes even faint internal body sounds — such as the heartbeat, breathing, and blood flow — clearly audible to the examiner.

 

• A standard (acoustic) stethoscope is a purely mechanical device that does not involve any electrical component, unlike modern electronic stethoscopes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The stethoscope was invented by René Laennec in 1816, initially as a simple wooden tube.

 

• Other everyday applications of the reflection of sound include megaphones (which direct sound in one direction) and SONAR (used to detect underwater objects and measure ocean depth).

 

• Electronic stethoscopes do convert sound into an electrical signal for amplification, but this is not the working principle of the traditional/standard stethoscope referred to here.

 

NOTE

 

• Conversion of sound into electric signals only (Option A): Describes electronic stethoscopes, not the basic acoustic principle used by a standard stethoscope.

 

• Absorption of high-frequency sound (Option C): Absorption would reduce the sound reaching the ears, which is the opposite of what a stethoscope is designed to do.

 

• Conversion of sound into light for observation (Option D): This is not a real physical process used in any stethoscope.

question: Electric current is expressed as:
option_1: rate of flow of electric charge
option_2: amount of charge per unit area
option_3: amount of charge per unit length
solution_text:
The correct answer is rate of flow of electric charge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electric current (I) is defined as the rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-section of a conductor, given by the formula I = Q/t, where Q is charge (in coulombs) and t is time (in seconds). (विद्युत धारा = आवेश प्रवाह की दर)

 

• The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A); a current of 1 ampere means 1 coulomb of charge flows past a point in 1 second.

 

• Conventionally, the direction of current is taken as the direction of flow of positive charge, which is opposite to the actual direction of flow of electrons in a metallic conductor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electric charge (Q) is measured in coulombs (C); the charge on one electron is approximately 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

 

• Current is measured using an ammeter, which is always connected in series in a circuit.

 

• Ohm's Law relates current, voltage and resistance: V = IR, where V is potential difference (volts), I is current (amperes), and R is resistance (ohms).

 

NOTE

 

• Amount of charge per unit area (Option B): This would describe a concept like current density (charge flow per unit cross-sectional area), not current itself.

 

• Amount of charge per unit length (Option C): This does not correspond to any standard electrical quantity relevant to current.

 

• Energy consumed per unit time (Option D): This describes electric power (P = VI), not electric current.

question: How does fumigation help in the safe storage of food grains?
option_1: It adds nutrients to the grains.
option_2: It prevents moisture loss from grains.
option_3: It increases the weight of the grains.
option_4: It kills pests and insects that could otherwise damage stored grains.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It kills pests and insects that could otherwise damage stored grains.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fumigation is the process of treating stored grains with chemical fumigants (toxic gases or vapours, such as aluminium phosphide or methyl bromide) that kill insects, pests, rodents and their eggs/larvae that infest and damage stored food grains. (धूम्रीकरण — अनाज में कीटों को नष्ट करना)

 

• Fumigants work by releasing gases within a sealed storage space (like a godown or silo) that are toxic to pests but which dissipate before the grain is used for consumption.

 

• This process significantly reduces post-harvest losses of food grains due to insect and pest infestation, which is a major concern for food security in a country like India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Proper grain storage combines fumigation with methods like keeping grains in cool, dry conditions, using airtight containers/silos, and adding substances like neem leaves as a natural pest deterrent.

 

• In India, the Food Corporation of India (FCI) is responsible for the procurement, storage, and distribution of foodgrains, and manages large storage facilities where fumigation and pest control are routinely used.

 

• Common storage pests include weevils, beetles and rodents, which can cause significant quantity and quality loss if grains are not properly protected.

 

NOTE

 

• It adds nutrients to the grains (Option A): Fumigation is a pest-control measure, not a nutritional treatment; it does not add any nutrients.

 

• It prevents moisture loss from grains (Option B): Moisture control is achieved through proper drying and sealed storage, not through fumigation.

 

• It increases the weight of the grains (Option C): Fumigation does not add mass to the grains; in fact, minimising pest damage helps preserve (not artificially increase) the grain's original weight.

question: When lead nitrate reacts with potassium iodide, a yellow precipitate of compound ‘X’ is formed. Identify compound X.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lead(II) iodide (PbI2).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a colourless solution of lead nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] is mixed with a colourless solution of potassium iodide (KI), a double displacement (precipitation) reaction occurs, producing a bright yellow precipitate of lead iodide (PbI₂), famously known as the 'golden rain' reaction. (लेड आयोडाइड — 'सुनहरी वर्षा' अभिक्रिया)

 

• The balanced chemical equation is: Pb(NO₃)₂ (aq) + 2KI (aq) → PbI₂ (s) [yellow ppt.] + 2KNO₃ (aq).

 

• This is a classic example of a precipitation reaction, where two soluble salts react in solution to form an insoluble solid (precipitate) — here, lead iodide, which is insoluble in water, settles out as a distinct yellow solid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a double displacement reaction, the positive and negative ions of two compounds exchange partners: here, Pb²⁺ combines with I⁻ (forming PbI₂), while K⁺ combines with NO₃⁻ (forming KNO₃, which stays dissolved).

 

• The 'golden rain' demonstration is a popular chemistry classroom experiment because slowly cooling the hot solution causes the yellow PbI₂ crystals to precipitate out dramatically, resembling falling gold flakes.

 

• Most nitrate salts are soluble in water, which is why potassium nitrate (the other product) remains dissolved rather than precipitating.

 

NOTE

 

• Lead(II) nitrate [Pb(NO3)2] (Option A): This is a reactant, not the product formed as a precipitate.

 

• Potassium nitrate (KNO3) (Option B): This is also a product of the reaction, but it remains soluble in solution and is not the yellow precipitate.

 

• Lead(II) nitrite [Pb(NO2)2] (Option C): This compound is not formed in this reaction at all; it is a distractor.

question: Which of the following alcohols is commonly used as a fuel or fuel additive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is widely used as a biofuel and fuel additive, commonly blended with petrol (as in India's Ethanol Blended Petrol/E20 programme) to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower vehicle emissions. (इथेनॉल — जैव ईंधन के रूप में प्रयोग)

 

• Ethanol is produced mainly by the fermentation of sugars derived from crops like sugarcane, maize, and other biomass, making it a renewable source of energy.

 

• Ethanol burns cleanly, has a high octane rating (which improves engine performance), and is a key component of India's push toward energy self-sufficiency and reduced carbon emissions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) achieved its 20% ethanol blending (E20) target ahead of schedule (originally targeted for 2025-26), reducing crude oil imports.

 

• Methanol (Option C) is also explored as an alternative fuel (e.g. in the NITI Aayog's Methanol Economy programme) but is more commonly used as an industrial solvent and is toxic if ingested.

 

• Both ethanol and methanol belong to the class of organic compounds called alcohols, characterised by the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group.

 

NOTE

 

• Propanol (Option A) and Butanol (Option B): These are used mainly as industrial solvents and in chemical manufacturing, not commonly as vehicle fuels in India.

 

• Methanol (Option C): Used in some industrial and experimental fuel applications, but it is toxic and not the standard fuel additive blended with petrol in India — that role belongs to ethanol.

question: A car starts to move from rest and attains a velocity of 20 m/s in 4 seconds. What is the acceleration of the car?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 m/s².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acceleration (a) is defined as the rate of change of velocity, given by the formula a = (v − u) / t, where u is initial velocity, v is final velocity, and t is time taken. (त्वरण = वेग में परिवर्तन की दर)

 

• Here, the car starts from rest, so initial velocity u = 0 m/s, final velocity v = 20 m/s, and time t = 4 s.

 

• a = (20 − 0) ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared (m/s²).

 

• Uniform acceleration means the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, which is assumed in this simple calculation.

 

• The three standard equations of motion — v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as — are all built on this same definition of acceleration.

 

NOTE

 

• 4 m/s2 (Option B): Would result from incorrectly using 20 ÷ 5 or a similar miscalculation, not the actual data given.

 

• 80 m/s2 (Option C): This comes from multiplying (20 × 4) instead of dividing, an incorrect operation.

 

• 100 m/s2 (Option D): Also an incorrect value not derived from the correct formula a = (v − u)/t with the given numbers.

question: Which of the following statements about electric field lines is correct?
option_4: They start on negative charges and end on positive charges
solution_text:
The correct answer is They never intersect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electric field lines never intersect (cross) each other. If two field lines were to cross, it would imply that the electric field at that point has two different directions simultaneously, which is physically impossible since the electric field at any point has a single, unique direction. (विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएँ — कभी प्रतिच्छेद नहीं करतीं)

 

• Electric field lines represent the direction a positive test charge would move if placed in the field, and their density (closeness) represents the strength/magnitude of the electric field at that location.

 

• Field lines are drawn to always point from positive charges toward negative charges (i.e., they originate on positive charges and terminate on negative charges).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electric field lines can be straight (as around a single point charge or between parallel plates) or curved (as around a dipole or non-symmetric charge configuration).

 

• Field lines are always perpendicular to the surface of a conductor at electrostatic equilibrium.

 

• The number of field lines emerging from or entering a charge is proportional to the magnitude of that charge, a concept formalised in Gauss's Law.

 

NOTE

 

• They can form closed loops (Option B): Incorrect for electrostatic field lines — they always begin on positive charge and end on negative charge (or at infinity), never forming closed loops (unlike magnetic field lines, which do form closed loops).

 

• They are always straight lines (Option C): Incorrect — field lines are often curved, depending on the charge configuration.

 

• They start on negative charges and end on positive charges (Option D): This is the reverse of the actual convention — field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges.

question: Which of the following is a function of the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manufacture of lipids.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) lacks ribosomes on its surface (unlike the rough ER) and is primarily involved in the synthesis of lipids (fats) and steroids, as well as the detoxification of drugs and poisons. (चिकनी अंतर्द्रव्यी जालिका — वसा संश्लेषण)

 

• SER is especially abundant in cells that secrete steroid hormones (e.g. cells of the adrenal cortex and gonads) and in liver cells, where it plays a key role in detoxifying harmful substances.

 

• SER is also involved in calcium ion storage and release in muscle cells (where it is specialised as the sarcoplasmic reticulum).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER), studded with ribosomes, is responsible for the synthesis of proteins that are meant for secretion or for use in membranes.

 

• The Golgi apparatus (Golgi body) is responsible for the modification, packaging, and sorting of proteins and lipids (including the modification of sugars/glycosylation) received from the ER, and dispatching them to their destinations.

 

• Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis and are assembled in the nucleolus of the cell nucleus, not by the ER.

 

NOTE

 

• Synthesis of proteins (Option A): This is a function of the Rough ER (due to attached ribosomes), not the Smooth ER.

 

• Assembly of ribosomes (Option C): Ribosomal subunits are assembled in the nucleolus, not in the ER.

 

• Modification of sugars (Option D): This function (glycosylation) primarily occurs in the Golgi apparatus, not the Smooth ER.

question: Which of the following is a biological method of crop protection?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Introducing pest predators.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biological control (biological method of crop protection) involves using natural enemies of pests — such as predators, parasites, or pathogens — to keep pest populations in check, without the use of synthetic chemicals. (जैविक नियंत्रण — प्राकृतिक शत्रुओं का उपयोग)

 

• Introducing pest predators (e.g. ladybird beetles to control aphids, or the parasitic wasp *Trichogramma* to control caterpillar pests) is a classic, eco-friendly example of biological pest control.

 

• This method is preferred for being environmentally sustainable, reducing chemical pesticide residue in food, and preventing the pests from developing resistance, unlike chemical methods.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other biological/eco-friendly approaches to crop protection include crop rotation, use of pest-resistant varieties, neem-based biopesticides, and integrated pest management (IPM), which combines multiple strategies.

 

• DDT (Dichloro-Diphenyl-Trichloroethane) is a synthetic chemical pesticide; although effective, it is now banned or restricted in many countries (including largely in India) due to its harmful, long-lasting environmental and health effects (bioaccumulation).

 

• Ploughing and burning crop residues are mechanical/physical farming practices, not biological methods — and stubble burning, in particular, is a major cause of air pollution in North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Ploughing (Option A): A mechanical/physical method of exposing pests and weeds to predators and weather, not a biological method itself.

 

• Burning crop residues (Option C): A harmful physical practice (stubble burning) associated with severe air pollution, and not a recommended crop protection method.

 

• Spraying DDT (Option D): This is a chemical method of pest control, the opposite of a biological method.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 3 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 12 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe fills the tank in 3 minutes; emptying pipe empties the full tank in 12 minutes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Filling pipe's rate = 1/3 tank/min. Emptying pipe's rate = 1/12 tank/min.

 

• Both opened together, net rate = 1/3 − 1/12 = 4/12 − 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 tank per minute.

 

• Time to fill the whole tank = 1 ÷ (1/4) = 4 minutes. Time to fill one-fourth of the tank = (1/4) ÷ (1/4 tank/min) = 1 minute.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net rate = 1/4 tank/min directly gives: filling exactly 1/4 of the tank takes exactly 1 minute, since the net rate itself is 1/4 tank per minute.

 

NOTE

 

• Always combine pipe rates as (filling rate − emptying rate) when pipes work against each other; never simply add or subtract the given times.

question: In an examination, the percentage of students who qualified from school X to the number of students who appeared from that school is 80%. In school Y, the number of students who appeared is 15% more than those from school X, and the number of students who qualified is 30% more than the number of students qualified from school X. What is the percentage of students qualified to the number of students who appeared from school Y (rounded off to one decimal place)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A).4% (i.e. 90.4%).

 

GIVEN

 

• School X: qualified/appeared = 80%. School Y: appeared = 15% more than X's appeared; qualified = 30% more than X's qualified.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let appeared in X = 100. Then qualified in X = 80% of 100 = 80.

 

• Appeared in Y = 100 × 1.15 = 115. Qualified in Y = 80 × 1.30 = 104.

 

• Required percentage = (Qualified in Y ÷ Appeared in Y) × 100 = (104 ÷ 115) × 100 = 90.43...% ≈ 90.4%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• New % = (Old% × (1 + qualified% change)) ÷ (1 + appeared% change) = (80 × 1.30) ÷ 1.15 = 104 ÷ 1.15 = 90.4%.

 

NOTE

 

• As printed in the source, the option text itself is truncated (e.g. 'A).4%' instead of 'A) 90.4%'); this has been reproduced exactly as it appears in the original paper. The computed value 90.4% matches Option 1's ending digits ('.4%').

question: If cos α = 5/13, where α is acute, find the value of sec α − tan α.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 1/5.

 

GIVEN

 

• cos α = 5/13, where α is acute.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since cos α = adjacent/hypotenuse = 5/13, this corresponds to a right triangle with sides 5, 12, 13 (a Pythagorean triplet), so opposite side = 12.

 

• sec α = hypotenuse/adjacent = 13/5. tan α = opposite/adjacent = 12/5.

 

• sec α − tan α = 13/5 − 12/5 = 1/5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For cos α = b/h (a Pythagorean triplet), sec α − tan α = (h − p)/b, where p is the perpendicular. Here = (13 − 12)/5 = 1/5.

 

NOTE

 

• Recognising 5-12-13 as a standard Pythagorean triplet instantly gives all trigonometric ratios without using formulas — memorise 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25 for speed.

question: In a group of 150 players consisting of males and females, 58% are males. The average weight of the male players is 82 kg, while that of the female players is 72 kg. Find the average weight (in kg) of all the players in the group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A).8 (i.e. 77.8 kg).

 

GIVEN

 

• Total players = 150; males = 58% (average weight 82 kg); females = 42% (average weight 72 kg).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number of males = 58% of 150 = 87. Number of females = 150 − 87 = 63.

 

• Total weight = (87 × 82) + (63 × 72) = 7,134 + 4,536 = 11,670 kg.

 

• Average weight of all players = 11,670 ÷ 150 = 77.8 kg.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Weighted average = 82 × (58/100) + 72 × (42/100) = 47.56 + 30.24 = 77.8 kg — a direct weighted-average shortcut without finding head-counts.

 

NOTE

 

• As printed in the source, the option text is truncated ('A).8' instead of 'A) 77.8'); reproduced exactly as in the original paper. The computed value 77.8 matches Option 1's ending digits ('.8').

question: Aakash, Suman and Raj invest ₹1,720, ₹1,690 and ₹1,240, respectively, to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹1,440, then what is the share of Raj in the profit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹384.

 

GIVEN

 

• Investments: Aakash = ₹1,720; Suman = ₹1,690; Raj = ₹1,240. Total profit = ₹1,440.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since all invested for the same time period, profit is shared in the ratio of their investments.

 

• Total investment = 1,720 + 1,690 + 1,240 = ₹4,650.

 

• Raj's share = (1,240 ÷ 4,650) × 1,440 = (1,240 × 1,440) ÷ 4,650 = 1,785,600 ÷ 4,650 = ₹384.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Simplify the investment ratio first: 1,720 : 1,690 : 1,240 = 172 : 169 : 124 (÷10); use this smaller ratio to divide 1,440 for faster mental calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• In a simple partnership (equal time period for all partners), profit-sharing ratio = investment ratio; time need only be considered when partners invest for different durations.

question: If a X m long train running at a speed of 59 m/sec crosses a railway platform in 9 sec. Find the value of X, if the length of the railway platform is 279 m.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 252.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = X m, speed = 59 m/s, time to cross platform = 9 s, platform length = 279 m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Distance covered while crossing the platform = speed × time = 59 × 9 = 531 m.

 

• This distance equals (train length + platform length): X + 279 = 531.

 

• X = 531 − 279 = 252.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Distance crossed = train length + platform length whenever a train crosses any stationary object longer than itself; just subtract the known length from total distance.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse 'crossing a platform' (needs train length + platform length) with 'crossing a man/pole' (needs only train length).

question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠ R and ∠ S meet at point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠ STR = 24°. If the ratio of ∠ P to ∠ Q is 3 : 5, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠ Q and ∠ P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 12°.

 

GIVEN

 

• In quadrilateral PQRS, bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at T; ∠STR = 24°. ∠P : ∠Q = 3 : 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Standard result: when the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S of a quadrilateral PQRS meet at T, ∠RTS = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2.

 

• So (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 = 24° ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 48°.

 

• With ∠P : ∠Q = 3 : 5, total parts = 8; 1 part = 48 ÷ 8 = 6°. So ∠P = 18°, ∠Q = 30°.

 

• Difference = ∠Q − ∠P = 30° − 18° = 12°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once ∠P + ∠Q = 48° is found, the difference for a 3 : 5 ratio = 48 × (5 − 3)/(5 + 3) = 48 × 2/8 = 12°, without separately finding each angle.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorise the result ∠RTS = (∠P + ∠Q)/2 for this common bisector-meeting-point quadrilateral question type — it saves significant time in the exam.

question: The average age of 40 students of a class is 33 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 34 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 74.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 40 students = 33 years. Including the teacher (41 people), average becomes 34 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ages of 40 students = 40 × 33 = 1,320 years.

 

• Sum of ages of all 41 people (students + teacher) = 41 × 34 = 1,394 years.

 

• Teacher's age = 1,394 − 1,320 = 74 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = old average + (number of students) × (increase in average) = 33 + 40 × 1 = 74 years.

 

NOTE

 

• When one new value joins a group and raises the average by 'd', the new value = old average + (old count) × d.

question: X people were given a contract for doing a piece of work in 28 days. 5 people did not turn up to work due to sickness, and the rest of the people completed the work in 30 days. What is the value of X?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 75.

 

GIVEN

 

• X people were to complete the work in 28 days; with 5 people absent, the rest completed it in 30 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total work = X × 28 man-days (using the original plan).

 

• With (X − 5) people, the same work takes 30 days: (X − 5) × 30 man-days.

 

• Equating: 28X = 30(X − 5) ⇒ 28X = 30X − 150 ⇒ 2X = 150 ⇒ X = 75.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ directly: X × 28 = (X−5) × 30; solve the linear equation in one step.

 

NOTE

 

• Total work (man-days) stays constant; only the number of workers and days change — this is the core idea behind all 'work and time' problems.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 84, then the result is the same number. 65% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A).25 (i.e. 68.25).

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number, added to 84, equals the number itself.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number be x. Then 0.20x + 84 = x.

 

• 84 = x − 0.20x = 0.80x ⇒ x = 84 ÷ 0.80 = 105.

 

• 65% of 105 = 0.65 × 105 = 68.25.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 84 represents 80% of the number (since 100% − 20% = 80%), so the number = 84 × (100/80) = 105; then take 65% of it directly.

 

NOTE

 

• As printed in the source, all four options appear identically truncated ('A).25', 'B).25', 'C).25', 'D).25'); reproduced exactly as in the original paper, even though this makes the printed options indistinguishable from one another. The computed value is 68.25.

question: A car travels from City A to City B, a distance of 150 km, at a speed of 60 km/hr. On the way back, due to heavy traffic, the car's speed decreases. If the total time for the round trip is 7 hours 30 min, what is the speed during the return trip?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 30 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Distance A to B = 150 km at 60 km/hr; total round-trip time = 7 hours 30 minutes = 7.5 hours.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time for onward journey = 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours.

 

• Time for return journey = 7.5 − 2.5 = 5 hours.

 

• Return speed = distance ÷ time = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert total time to hours first (7h30min = 7.5h), subtract the known onward time, then divide the same distance by the remaining time.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert mixed time units (hours and minutes) into a single unit (decimal hours) before doing speed-time-distance calculations.

question: A manufacturer sells a transistor for ₹840 at a gain of 20% to a shopkeeper. The shopkeeper then sells it to a customer at a profit of 10%. What is the difference between the cost price to the manufacturer and the cost price to the customer (in ₹)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 224.

 

GIVEN

 

• Manufacturer sells at ₹840 (20% gain). Shopkeeper resells at 10% profit.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Manufacturer's cost price: SP = ₹840 at 20% gain ⇒ CP(manufacturer) = 840 ÷ 1.20 = ₹700.

 

• Shopkeeper's selling price (= customer's cost price) at 10% profit on ₹840: 840 × 1.10 = ₹924.

 

• Difference = 924 − 700 = ₹224.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• CP = SP × 100/(100+profit%). Manufacturer's CP = 840 × 100/120 = 700; Customer's CP = 840 × 110/100 = 924; difference = 224.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Cost price to the customer' means the price the customer pays (i.e., the shopkeeper's selling price) — a common point of confusion in chain profit-loss questions.

question: Thomas is 38 years old. His nephew is 26 years younger than him. In how many years will Thomas's age be 14 years less than three times his nephew's age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 8.

 

GIVEN

 

• Thomas's present age = 38 years. Nephew's present age = 38 − 26 = 12 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the required number of years be n. After n years: Thomas's age = 38 + n; nephew's age = 12 + n.

 

• Condition: Thomas's age = 3 × nephew's age − 14 ⇒ 38 + n = 3(12 + n) − 14.

 

• 38 + n = 36 + 3n − 14 = 22 + 3n ⇒ 38 − 22 = 3n − n ⇒ 16 = 2n ⇒ n = 8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Translate the condition directly into one linear equation in n and solve — avoid trial-and-error with the options, which is slower for age problems with a '3 times' condition.

 

NOTE

 

• Always define ages 'n years from now' as (present age + n) for both people, and translate the word condition into an equation carefully before solving.

question: The LCM of two numbers is four times their HCF. The sum of their LCM and HCF is 140. If one of the numbers is 112, find the other number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 28.

 

GIVEN

 

• LCM = 4 × HCF. LCM + HCF = 140. One number = 112.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let HCF = h. Then LCM = 4h. So h + 4h = 140 ⇒ 5h = 140 ⇒ h = 28. So HCF = 28, LCM = 4 × 28 = 112.

 

• Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF = 112 × 28 = 3,136.

 

• Other number = 3,136 ÷ 112 = 28.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Product of two numbers always equals LCM × HCF; once both are found, just divide the product by the known number to get the other.

 

NOTE

 

• Interestingly here, LCM = 112 exactly equals the given number, and the other number also works out to 28 = HCF — a special coincidence worth double-checking, not a general rule.

question: Prakhar and Riya together invested ₹33,500 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹6,700, Prakhar's share was ₹2,000. What was Prakhar's investment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹10,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment = ₹33,500. Total profit = ₹6,700. Prakhar's share of profit = ₹2,000.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In a partnership (same time period), profit share ratio = investment ratio.

 

• Prakhar's investment ÷ Total investment = Prakhar's profit ÷ Total profit.

 

• Prakhar's investment = (2,000 ÷ 6,700) × 33,500 = 2,000 × 5 = ₹10,000 (since 33,500 ÷ 6,700 = 5).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice 33,500 ÷ 6,700 = 5 exactly, so every profit share simply multiplies by 5 to get the corresponding investment — Prakhar's investment = 2,000 × 5 = 10,000.

 

NOTE

 

• Look for a simple multiplying factor between total investment and total profit before doing longer fraction calculations — it often shortcuts the arithmetic.

question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article at ₹5,360. Find the cost price if after allowing a discount of 8% he still gains 34% on the cost price.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹3,680.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price (MP) = ₹5,360. Discount = 8%. Gain = 34% on cost price (CP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling price (SP) after discount = MP × (1 − 8/100) = 5,360 × 0.92 = ₹4,931.20.

 

• Since SP = CP × (1 + 34/100) = 1.34 × CP: CP = 4,931.20 ÷ 1.34.

 

• CP = ₹3,680 (verify: 3,680 × 1.34 = 4,931.20 ✓).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• CP = MP × (100 − discount%) ÷ (100 + gain%) = 5,360 × 92/134 = 3,680, in a single step.

 

NOTE

 

• Discount is always calculated on the marked price, while profit/gain is always calculated on the cost price — never mix up the two bases.

question: The value of 999.99 + 99.99 + 9.99 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. D).97 (i.e. 1109.97).

 

GIVEN

 

• 999.99 + 99.99 + 9.99 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Write each number as (next whole number − 0.01): 999.99 = 1000 − 0.01; 99.99 = 100 − 0.01; 9.99 = 10 − 0.01.

 

• Sum = (1000 + 100 + 10) − (0.01 × 3) = 1110 − 0.03 = 1109.97.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For numbers ending in '.99', round each up to the next whole number, add, then subtract 0.01 for every number rounded — much faster than direct column addition.

 

NOTE

 

• As printed in the source, the option text is truncated ('D).97' instead of 'D) 1109.97'); reproduced exactly as in the original paper. The computed value 1109.97 matches Option 4's ending digits ('.97').

question:
Arrange the following schemes in the ascending order of their discounts.

 

A. Buy 5 get 6 free.

B. A single discount of 82%.

C. Two successive discounts of 11% and 24%.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. C, A, B.

 

GIVEN

 

• Scheme A: buy 5, get 6 free (11 items for the price of 5). Scheme B: single discount 82%. Scheme C: successive discounts 11% and 24%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scheme A: pay for 5 items, receive 11 items total ⇒ effective discount = 6/11 × 100 = 54.55%.

 

• Scheme B: straightforward single discount = 82%.

 

• Scheme C (successive discounts): net discount = 1 − (1 − 0.11)(1 − 0.24) = 1 − (0.89 × 0.76) = 1 − 0.6764 = 32.36%.

 

• Ascending order (lowest to highest discount): C (32.36%) < A (54.55%) < B (82%), i.e., C, A, B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Successive discount formula: net% = x + y − (xy/100). For 11% and 24%: 11 + 24 − (11×24)/100 = 35 − 2.64 = 32.36%.

 

NOTE

 

• Never simply add successive discount percentages directly (11% + 24% ≠ 35% net) — always use the successive-discount formula, since the second discount applies to an already-reduced price.

question: Water flows through a cylindrical pipe of diameter 14 cm at a speed of 15 km/hr into a rectangular tank 50 m long and 44 m wide. How long will it take for the water level in the tank to rise by 21 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2 hours.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pipe diameter = 14 cm (radius = 7 cm = 0.07 m); flow speed = 15 km/hr; tank = 50 m × 44 m; rise required = 21 cm = 0.21 m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Cross-sectional area of pipe = πr² = (22/7) × 0.07 × 0.07 = 0.0154 m².

 

• Volume of water flowing per hour = area × speed = 0.0154 × 15,000 = 231 m³/hr.

 

• Volume needed to raise tank level by 0.21 m = 50 × 44 × 0.21 = 462 m³.

 

• Time = 462 ÷ 231 = 2 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert all lengths to the same unit (metres) first; then Time = (Tank base area × rise) ÷ (Pipe cross-section area × speed) in one clean formula.

 

NOTE

 

• A very common slip is forgetting to convert cm to m (diameter and rise) before using them alongside speed in km/hr — always match units before calculating.

question: A sum of money was invested at simple interest at a certain rate for 4 years. Had it been invested at a 3% per annum higher rate, it would have fetched ₹960 more. Find the principal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ₹8,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Time = 4 years; a 3% higher annual rate yields ₹960 more in simple interest.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Extra SI = (Principal × extra rate × time) ÷ 100 ⇒ 960 = (P × 3 × 4) ÷ 100.

 

• 960 = 12P/100 ⇒ P = 960 × 100 ÷ 12 = ₹8,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Extra SI depends only on the extra rate and time, not the original rate — directly use Extra SI = P × (rate difference) × time / 100 to solve for P.

 

NOTE

 

• In such 'higher rate would have fetched more' problems, the original rate is irrelevant and need not (and cannot) be found — only the rate difference matters.

question: If a + 1/a = 12, then find the value of a² + 1/a².
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 142.

 

GIVEN

 

• a + 1/a = 12.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Squaring both sides: (a + 1/a)² = a² + 2(a)(1/a) + 1/a² = a² + 1/a² + 2.

 

• So 12² = a² + 1/a² + 2 ⇒ 144 = a² + 1/a² + 2.

 

• a² + 1/a² = 144 − 2 = 142.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Standard identity: if a + 1/a = k, then a² + 1/a² = k² − 2. Here k² − 2 = 144 − 2 = 142 directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorise the algebraic identities a² + 1/a² = (a+1/a)² − 2 and a³ + 1/a³ = (a+1/a)³ − 3(a+1/a) — they appear frequently in RRB exams.

question: Simplify: (2^4)^3 × (2^5)^2 ÷ 2^7
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 215 (i.e. 2^15).

 

GIVEN

 

• (2⁴)³ × (2⁵)² ÷ 2⁷ = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Apply the power-of-a-power rule (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ: (2⁴)³ = 2¹², and (2⁵)² = 2¹⁰.

 

• Multiply (same base, add exponents): 2¹² × 2¹⁰ = 2²².

 

• Divide (same base, subtract exponents): 2²² ÷ 2⁷ = 2^(22−7) = 2¹⁵.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Just add/subtract the exponents directly: (4×3) + (5×2) − 7 = 12 + 10 − 7 = 15, so the answer is 2¹⁵ in one line, without expanding any power.

 

NOTE

 

• As printed in the source, the options omit the exponent symbol (e.g. '215' instead of '2^15' or '2¹⁵'); reproduced exactly as in the original paper. The correct value is 2 raised to the power 15, matching Option 1.

question: Ravi's father is 4 times as old as Ravi. After 5 years, the father's age will be 3 times Ravi's age. What is Ravi's present age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 10 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Father's present age = 4 × Ravi's present age. After 5 years, father's age = 3 × Ravi's age (at that time).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Ravi's present age = r. Father's present age = 4r.

 

• After 5 years: 4r + 5 = 3(r + 5) = 3r + 15.

 

• 4r + 5 = 3r + 15 ⇒ r = 15 − 5 = 10 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Translate both age conditions into a single linear equation in one unknown (Ravi's present age) — with only one variable, the equation solves in one step.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify: Ravi = 10, Father = 40 now; after 5 years, Ravi = 15, Father = 45 = 3 × 15 ✓ — a quick sanity check that costs little time and catches setup errors.

question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 528 m2 and its volume is 1848 m3. Find the total surface area (in m2) of the cylinder. (Take π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 836.

 

GIVEN

 

• Curved surface area (CSA) = 528 m², Volume = 1,848 m³, π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CSA = 2πrh = 528, and Volume = πr²h = 1,848.

 

• Dividing Volume by CSA: (πr²h) ÷ (2πrh) = r/2 = 1,848 ÷ 528 = 3.5 ⇒ r = 7 m.

 

• From CSA: 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 528 ⇒ 44h = 528 ⇒ h = 12 m.

 

• Total surface area = 2πr(h + r) = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (12 + 7) = 44 × 19 = 836 m².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Dividing Volume by CSA always gives r/2 directly (since πr²h ÷ 2πrh = r/2) — a fast way to extract the radius without solving two equations separately.

 

NOTE

 

• TSA = CSA + 2 × (area of two circular bases) = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r); don't forget to add the two circular ends when finding total (not curved) surface area.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 10/100?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 50%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find what percentage 1/20 is of 10/100.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert both to decimals: 1/20 = 0.05, and 10/100 = 0.10.

 

• Required percentage = (0.05 ÷ 0.10) × 100 = 50%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 1/20 = 5% and 10/100 = 10%; so the question reduces to 'what % is 5 of 10?' = 50%, avoiding fraction division altogether.

 

NOTE

 

• 'A is what percentage of B' always means (A ÷ B) × 100 — keep the order of numerator and denominator straight to avoid an inverted answer.

question: Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K and L are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only I is kept above C. Only L is kept between C and J. Only K is kept below D. How many boxes are kept between B and I?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes B, C, D, I, J, K, L stacked. Only I is above C. Only L is between C and J. Only K is below D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only I is above C' ⇒ I is directly above C, and nothing else is above C. So from the top: Position 1 = I, Position 2 = C.

 

• 'Only L is between C and J', and since nothing can be above C (as established), J must be below C, with exactly L in between: Position 3 = L, Position 4 = J.

 

• 'Only K is below D' ⇒ K is at the very bottom (Position 7), and D is just above it: Position 6 = D, Position 7 = K.

 

• The only box left, B, takes the one remaining slot: Position 5 = B.

 

• Final order (top to bottom): I, C, L, J, B, D, K. Boxes between B (position 5) and I (position 1) = C, L, J = Three boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In stacking puzzles, phrases like 'Only X is above/below Y' fix an exact position — place these anchor clues first, then slot in the remaining elements by elimination.

 

NOTE

 

• Draw the stack as a vertical list of 7 blank slots and fill from the strongest ('only ... above/below') clues inward — this avoids losing track of relative order.

question:
If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’ , ‘B’ stands for ‘x’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘-‘ , what will come in place of the question mark ‘?’ in the following equation?

 

10 B 2 C 7 D 8 A 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 23.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Equation: 10 B 2 C 7 D 8 A 2 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 10 × 2 + 7 − 8 ÷ 2 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS — division first: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Multiplication: 10 × 2 = 20.

 

• Now: 20 + 7 − 4 = 27 − 4 = 23.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Substitute all letter-codes first to convert the whole expression into a normal arithmetic equation, then apply BODMAS in one pass — avoid solving symbol by symbol.

 

NOTE

 

• Always re-check which letter maps to which sign before substituting; a swapped mapping (e.g., mixing up A and D) is the most common error in this question type.

question:
Select the triad which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two triads given below. Both triads follow the same pattern.

 

NG-LE-JL

KD-IB-GI
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QJ-OH-MO.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triad 1: NG-LE-JL. Triad 2: KD-IB-GI. Find the option that follows the same pattern.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert to alphabet positions. Triad 1: NG (N=14,G=7); LE (L=12,E=5); JL (J=10,L=12).

 

• Both letters of group 2 = both letters of group 1 minus 2: (14−2,7−2)=(12,5)=LE ✓. Group 3's first letter = group 2's first letter minus 2 = 12−2=10=J; group 3's second letter = group 2's first letter = 12 = L. So group 3 = JL ✓.

 

• Confirm with Triad 2: KD(K=11,D=4) → group2 = (9,2) = IB ✓ → group3 = (9−2, 9) = (7,9) = GI ✓. Pattern confirmed: group2 = group1 − 2 (each letter); group3 = (group2's 1st letter − 2, group2's 1st letter).

 

• Test Option C: QJ(Q=17,J=10) → group2 = (15,8) = OH ✓ (matches given 'OH') → group3 = (15−2,15) = (13,15) = MO ✓ (matches given 'MO'). Both match!

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once you spot 'each letter of the first group minus 2 gives the second group', quickly verify only the second group of each option against the given triads before checking the third group.

 

NOTE

 

• In letter-triad questions, always convert to numeric alphabet positions (A=1...Z=26) first — patterns that look confusing in letters often become simple arithmetic (+/−) in numbers.

question: In a certain code language, ‘CLAW’ is coded as ‘3948’ and ‘FLAW’ is coded as ‘9748’. What is the code for ‘F’ in that language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• CLAW → 3948. FLAW → 9748.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CLAW and FLAW share three common letters — L, A, W — and differ only in the first letter (C vs F).

 

• Codes of CLAW = {3, 9, 4, 8}; codes of FLAW = {9, 7, 4, 8}. The digits {9, 4, 8} are common to both codes (these belong to the common letters L, A, W).

 

• The digit left over in CLAW's code (not in FLAW's) is 3, so C = 3. The digit left over in FLAW's code (not in CLAW's) is 7, so F = 7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two coded words share most letters and differ in just one, compare the two code strings: the digit that appears in only one code corresponds to the one letter that differs.

 

NOTE

 

• This 'compare and eliminate common digits' method is much faster than trying to build a full letter-to-digit cipher table from scratch.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

23 40 57 74 91 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 108.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 23, 40, 57, 74, 91, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 40−23=17; 57−40=17; 74−57=17; 91−74=17.

 

• The series increases by a constant 17 each time (a simple arithmetic progression).

 

• Next term = 91 + 17 = 108.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the first two differences match, assume a constant common difference and simply add it once more — no need to check every gap in a clean AP series.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the common difference across at least 3-4 consecutive pairs before finalising, in case the series later changes pattern (not the case here, but a good habit).

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DG-BE.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: FI-DH, JM-HL, HK-FJ, DG-BE.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert to alphabet positions and find the letter-wise difference within each pair.

 

• FI-DH: F(6)→D(4), diff = 2; I(9)→H(8), diff = 1.

 

• JM-HL: J(10)→H(8), diff = 2; M(13)→L(12), diff = 1.

 

• HK-FJ: H(8)→F(6), diff = 2; K(11)→J(10), diff = 1.

 

• DG-BE: D(4)→B(2), diff = 2; G(7)→E(5), diff = 2 (not 1, breaking the pattern).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to numbers and check both letters' differences for each pair — the pattern here is 'first letter −2, second letter −1'; find the pair where the second difference doesn't match.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Odd one out' letter questions almost always reduce to simple, consistent addition/subtraction patterns once converted to numeric alphabet positions.

question:
A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting in a straight line, facing the north.

Only two people sit to the right of X. Only two people sit between X and C. Only two people sit between A and D. D sits to the immediate left of X. B sits to the immediate right of Y.

Who sits at the third position from the left end of the line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. W.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people A, B, C, D, W, X, Y in a line facing north. Clues about X's position, distances, and immediate neighbours (as stated in the question).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two people sit to the right of X' ⇒ X is at position 5 (from the left, out of 7 seats).

 

• 'D sits to the immediate left of X' ⇒ D is at position 4.

 

• 'Only two people between X and C' ⇒ C is 3 seats from X ⇒ C is at position 2 (since position 8 doesn't exist).

 

• 'Only two people between A and D' ⇒ A is 3 seats from D (position 4) ⇒ A is at position 1 or 7.

 

• Remaining seats {1, 3, 6, 7} are for A, B, W, Y, with B immediately right of Y. Testing A = 1: remaining {3, 6, 7} for B, W, Y with B = Y+1 ⇒ Y = 6, B = 7, so W = 3 (this works). Testing A = 7 leaves {1,3,6} with no valid consecutive Y,B pair, so it is rejected.

 

• Final arrangement (left to right): A(1), C(2), W(3), D(4), X(5), Y(6), B(7). The third position from the left = W.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the person with a direct positional clue (X at position 5 here) first, then use 'immediate left/right' clues before working through the 'people between' clues.

 

NOTE

 

• Always test both possibilities when a clue like 'A is 3 seats from D' gives two options — one usually gets eliminated by a later clue, as happened here with A = 7.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means ‘A is the father of B’,

A - B means ‘A is the mother of B’,

A * B means ‘A is the sister of B’ and

A ÷ B means ‘A is the brother of B’.

Based on the above, how is P related to T if ‘P – Q * R + S ÷ T’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Father's mother.

 

GIVEN

 

• P – Q means P is mother of Q. Q * R means Q is sister of R. R + S means R is father of S. S ÷ T means S is brother of T.

 

SOLUTION

 

• P – Q: P is Q's mother. Q * R: Q is R's sister (same parents), so P is also R's mother.
